tagline.text: A night boat tour through the firefly-lit mangroves of a Puerto Princesa river

location.label: Location
location.text: Ferry area at Km 20, South National Highway, Iwahig, Puerto Princesa City

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱600–1,650 (from one boat for a self-arranged visit to a per-person tour with dinner)

children.text: On the Iwahig River, about
35 minutes
by road from Puerto Princesa city proper, you board a small boat after dark to watch fireflies in the mangroves. It is run by a community association, and each boat carries three passengers for about
45 minutes
on the river.

The Iwahig Firefly Watching tour is an evening boat experience on the riverbank of Iwahig village, south of Puerto Princesa in Palawan. Travelers usually fit it in after a big daytime outing such as the Underground River or Honda Bay, to fill the hours after sunset. The official Puerto Princesa city tourism site lists it as a program run by the Iwahig Community Ecotourism Association, and says that colonies of fireflies light up the riverbanks and that their presence is a sign of a healthy river ecosystem.
The boarding station is at the ferry area at Km 20 of the South National Highway in Iwahig. According to the city tourism site, it takes about
35 minutes
from the city proper by air-conditioned van. The watch opens at
6 PM
, and the boat fee is
for up to three people per boat. Life vests are reportedly provided, but please confirm on site.

You approach the riverbank quietly in a small boat guided by a boatman (the quiet operation comes from one booking site's description, so confirm on site) and see fireflies on the mangrove trees flashing together at close range. One traveler's account says the fireflies seemed to flash in response to the boatman's voice, glowing plankton lit up when the water was stirred, and on a clear night the boatman pointed out constellations with a laser pointer. That account dates from 2013, so things may differ today.

Going with a tour operator bundles hotel pickup, the boat and dinner and is convenient, while going on your own is much cheaper but means arranging night transport and dinner yourself. The boat ride lasts only about
45 minutes
, so it is best treated as a modest, quiet evening of firefly watching rather than something to expect too much from.
After sunset, fireflies perched in the mangroves on both banks make whole trees flash. The city tourism site explains that seeing fireflies is evidence of a healthy river ecosystem.

blocks.title: Close-up viewing from a small boat

children.text: Each boat carries up to three people, and the boatman quietly paddles close to the trees. Unlike watching from a distance on a large boat, you can clearly see the rhythm and flashing of the lights.

The operator is the Iwahig Community Ecotourism Association, which the city tourism site says has received a Philippine tourism award (PATA Gold). Boat fees go to local residents, so you can enjoy the trip and support conservation at the same time.

blocks.title: Glowing plankton and the night sky

children.text: According to travelers' accounts, stirring the water makes bioluminescent plankton sparkle, and on a cloudless night the boatman may point out constellations. This depends on weather and moonlight, so treat it as a bonus.

blocks.title: A good evening add-on to daytime trips

children.text: It fits neatly after a full day at the Underground River or Honda Bay, once the sun has set. Tour packages usually leave around
6 PM
and return within 3–4 hours.

blocks.title: Both tours and independent visits work

children.text: Tours with dinner and hotel pickup start at about ₱1,650, while going on your own means ₱600 per boat plus a van or tricycle. Choose whichever suits your group size and schedule.
You board a van at your hotel. One operator says it picks up between
, so get the exact time and a contact number when you book.
You arrive at the boarding station near Iwahig and wait for your number to be called. There are almost no restaurants there at night, so check in advance whether dinner is included.
Three people board each boat and head out to the mangrove riverbank. The boat ride lasts about
45 minutes
After watching the fireflies, you have dinner if your package includes it, then return to your hotel. The whole outing is generally described as taking 3–4 hours.

Schedules and order differ by operator, so the times above are only an example. Always follow the instructions for the tour you booked. Packages with hotel pickup and dinner cost more but handle transport and the meal in one go, and they leave less time flexibility than going on your own.

items.title: Independent route
items.subtitle: By van or tricycle from the city

children.text: Have dinner in the city first. Reviews say there are no restaurants near the boarding station.
Hire a van or tricycle and set off for the ferry area at Km 20 in Iwahig. It takes about
35 minutes
from the city.
The station is open from
6 PM
, so arrive early and check your turn. The association's phone numbers are 717-8035 and 0908-562-0040.
Up to three people ride in one boat for
. A group of four or more must split into separate boats.
You return to the city in the same vehicle. Few vehicles pass at night, so arrange your ride back with the driver in advance.
Reviews say it is hard to find public transport back from the boarding station, so it is safest to have your driver wait or to book a round trip.
There are direct flights from Manila to Puerto Princesa International Airport (PPS), taking around
1 hour 40 minutes
. Airlines and schedules change with the season.
From the airport to the city, you can take a short tricycle or taxi ride. Getting to Iwahig normally means passing through the city.
Check the latest flight times and fares when you book.

items.title: Van from the city to the boarding station

children.text: The city tourism site recommends air-conditioned vans from licensed tourist transport providers and lists a van rate of ₱1,500 for 10 passengers.
It is about
35 minutes
from the city, and the destination is the ferry area at Km 20 of the South National Highway in Iwahig.

items.title: Going by tricycle on your own

children.text: A 2013 account says the traveler hired a tricycle driver for about ₱500–700 round trip, and the ride took 30–45 minutes. The current fare may vary with bargaining.
Reviews say the road is dark at night and rough in places. There is practically no public transport at night, so make sure you have a ride back.

Many tours include hotel pickup. Some operators say they pick up only from lodging within 5 km of the airport, while others limit pickup to the city proper, so tell them where you are staying and confirm.
The tour runs all year, and fireflies can be seen from about
6 PM
after sunset. The lights are said to be clearest around the new moon, and may be less distinct under a full moon.
Rainy nights can make operations difficult. The rainy season in Puerto Princesa is generally
June–October

, so during that time schedule the tour earlier in your trip rather than on the last day, leaving room to postpone. Check on the day with the association or your booked operator whether it is running.
Allow about 3–4 hours in total on a hotel pickup tour, or about 3 hours including the round trip from the city if you go on your own. The time actually watching fireflies from the boat is about
45 minutes
, so it matters to arrive early and get your turn. Cloudy skies may rule out stargazing, so think of the stars as a bonus on clear nights.

The easiest plan is to stay in Puerto Princesa city and fit the firefly tour into an evening. Many tours include van pickup from your hotel, and restaurants and lodging cluster around the Baywalk.

Reviews say there are no restaurants near the boarding station, so if you go on your own, eat dinner in the city first. Some tours advertise dinner on the boat, but the food is rated as average, so keep expectations low. In the city you can enjoy seafood restaurants and local Palawan dishes.

A few planning tips: in Puerto Princesa, many days are spent at the Underground River or Honda Bay, so evenings can feel tiring. The firefly boat does not take long on the water and requires little exertion, so it is a light way to end the day. However, you may return to your hotel late, so if you have an early-morning departure the next day, move the firefly tour to the day before or to a day with more slack. Tours with hotel pickup run on fixed times, while going on your own gives you freedom but means arranging transport yourself, so choose according to your group size and stamina.
Flash photography is prohibited. It startles the insects, so turn off camera flashes and phone flashlights. Photos rarely come out in the dark, so it is best to enjoy it with your eyes.
Bring long sleeves and mosquito repellent. Mosquitoes are plentiful around the mangroves at dusk.
If you go on your own, arrive early and get your number. Reviews say that if you miss your call, your place may go to later arrivals.
A boat holds three people, so a group of four needs two boats. A group of three is the most economical.
For hotel pickup tours, get the exact pickup time and the operator's phone number when you book. A few reviews mention missed pickups.
Choose a clear night around the new moon. The weaker the moonlight, the clearer the fireflies.
Bring a light jacket and comfortable shoes. It can be windy over the river at night.
Do not touch or break the trees or plants. Protecting the firefly habitat is the premise of this kind of tourism.
Because this is a night outing, secure your ride back in advance, and on rainy days check on the day whether it is operating.
Some sources advise against it for pregnant women, people with limited mobility and people with severe insect allergies.
The boat ride lasts only about
45 minutes
, and some reviews say it is poor value for the price. Treat it as a modest evening experience rather than something to expect too much from.
Prices and operating hours differ by operator and change often. Check the latest notices.
The official site gives no closing time. Do not go too late; go in the early evening after
6 PM
Flash photography and touching the trees are prohibited, and you must follow the boatman's instructions.
About
35 minutes
by road from the boarding station, with lodging and restaurants. The Baywalk is also pleasant at dusk.
It is common to visit the Underground River by day and follow with the firefly tour in the evening. Leave plenty of margin for travel time and booking times.
It suits the evening after a day of island hopping. If it rains, boats may all be cancelled, so keep a spare day.
